editorial:
Imagine spending your days staring out your window, watching your neighbors just to kill time. That is exactly what Mr. Piero does in this slow-burn drama. He is a curious man who gets obsessed with Giovanni, a soldier who just moved into the building across the street. While Piero's wife thinks he is being ridiculous and the rest of the neighborhood mocks him, he cannot stop spying. The vibe starts off as a simple story about a bored man, but it quickly turns tense when Piero notices something scary. He sees that Giovanni came back from the war with blood on his hands, and suddenly, his little hobby feels a lot more dangerous.

What really works here is how the movie builds a feeling of worry without needing huge explosions or fast chases. The acting is solid and makes you feel Piero's growing panic. Some people might find the pace a bit slow, but if you like mysteries that sneak up on you, this is a great pick. You should definitely try to find a high-quality version to see the details of the rooms.
endingExplained: The story reaches a breaking point when Piero's spying finally reveals the truth about Giovanni's past. It turns out that the blood Piero saw was a sign of the terrible things Giovanni did during the war. The movie ends by showing that watching others can lead to truths that are too heavy to handle. Piero realizes his curiosity has trapped him in a nightmare, leaving you to wonder if some secrets are better left alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and character studies.
